soc-mov-01-c1.text: Matthew Radburn and Clifford Stott (2019). Riots Are Not Just Mindless Violence. Social Science Space (first published in The Conversation).

soc-mov-01-c1.claim: Both stories still endure in the popular imagination: the "mad mob", in which ordinary people lose their reason, and the "bad mob", in which criminals find each other.

soc-mov-01-c2.text: Matthew Radburn and Clifford Stott (2019). Riots Are Not Just Mindless Violence. Social Science Space (first published in The Conversation).

soc-mov-01-c2.claim: The police were attacked only inside St Pauls and were left alone once they had left.

soc-mov-01-c3.text: Christian Jarrett (2009). Emergencies inspire crowd cooperation, not panic. BPS Research Digest.
soc-mov-01-c3.quote: Twelve of the disaster victims described feelings of unity among the crowd, whereas nine of them said it was more a case of everyone for themselves.
soc-mov-01-c3.claim: Twelve described a feeling of unity in the crowd, and those twelve also reported more helping, even of strangers, and more orderliness, such as queuing to escape.

soc-mov-01-c3.text: Christian Jarrett (2013). Police and safety professionals fall for myths about people’s behaviour in emergencies. BPS Research Digest.
soc-mov-01-c3.quote: Overall, the police endorsed several aspects of the mass panic myth, including the idea that crowds tend to exaggerate the threat; that emotions and instincts overcome rational thought; and that fear and rumours spread like a contagion.
soc-mov-01-c3.claim: In a 2013 survey by Drury, David Novelli and Clifford Stott of 115 police personnel, 46 civilian emergency planners and 120 football stewards, the police endorsed several parts of the mass panic myth, such as the idea that fear and rumour spread like a contagion.

soc-mov-02-c1.text: Alan J. Kuperman (2008). Relative Deprivation. International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences (via Encyclopedia.com).

soc-mov-02-c1.claim: Yet the poorest and most oppressed groups are often quiet, and revolts are typically launched by groups whose conditions are rising, not falling.

soc-mov-02-c1.text: M. Brewster Smith (1968). Stouffer, Samuel A. International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences (via Encyclopedia.com).

soc-mov-02-c1.claim: The Air Force private, in a service with rapid promotion, felt more deprived than the private in the Military Police, where promotions were rare.

soc-mov-02-c2.text: National Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders (1968). Report of the National Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders. Internet Archive.
soc-mov-02-c2.quote: Characteristically, the typical rioter was not a hoodlum, habitual criminal, or riffraff; nor was he a recent migrant, a member of an uneducated underclass, or a person lacking broad social and political concerns.
soc-mov-02-c2.claim: The typical rioter was not a hoodlum, a habitual criminal or riffraff, nor a recent migrant.

soc-mov-02-c2.text: Alan J. Kuperman (2008). Relative Deprivation. International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences (via Encyclopedia.com).
soc-mov-02-c2.quote: Prominent economists and political scientists, including Paul Collier, Anke Hoeffler, David Laitin, and Jim Fearon, have disputed the primary role of relative deprivation in motivating rebellion, which they say is driven less by grievance than by greed.
soc-mov-02-c2.claim: Some economists and political scientists, including Paul Collier, Anke Hoeffler, David Laitin and James Fearon, have gone further and disputed that grievance is the main driver of rebellion at all, arguing that it is driven less by grievance than by greed.

soc-mov-03-c1.text: John Scott and Gordon Marshall (eds) (2009). resource mobilization. A Dictionary of Sociology (via Encyclopedia.com).
soc-mov-03-c1.quote: Resource mobilization stresses rationality, and the importance of adequate funding, leadership, and organization.
soc-mov-03-c1.claim: Resource mobilisation stressed rationality, and the importance of funding, leadership and organisation.

soc-mov-03-c2.text: Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute, Stanford University. Parks, Rosa. The Martin Luther King, Jr. Encyclopedia.

soc-mov-03-c2.claim: In 1943 she had joined the local chapter of the NAACP and been elected its secretary, and the summer before her arrest she attended a workshop on desegregation at the Highlander Folk School in Tennessee.

soc-mov-03-c2.text: Martin Luther King, Jr. Research and Education Institute, Stanford University. Montgomery Bus Boycott. The Martin Luther King, Jr. Encyclopedia.
soc-mov-03-c2.quote: On 5 December, 90 percent of Montgomery’s black citizens stayed off the buses.
soc-mov-03-c2.claim: Black ministers backed a one-day boycott on 5 December, and that day 90 percent of Montgomery's Black citizens stayed off the buses.

soc-mov-03-c3.text: Mark Engler and Paul Engler (2014). Can disruptive power create new social movements?. openDemocracy.
soc-mov-03-c3.quote: Poor People’s Movements irked both resource mobilization theorists and on-the-ground activists by contending that not only did formal structures fail to produce disruptive outbreaks, but that these structures actually detracted from mass protest when it did occur.
soc-mov-03-c3.claim: Formal organisations did not produce these outbreaks, they argued, and often blunted them.

soc-mov-06-c1.text: Michelle Nicholasen (2019). Why nonviolent resistance beats violent force in effecting social, political change. Harvard Gazette.

soc-mov-06-c1.claim: With Maria Stephan she spent two years collecting data on every violent and nonviolent campaign from 1900 to 2006 that sought to overthrow a government or win territorial liberation

soc-mov-06-c1.text: Erica Chenoweth (2020). The Future of Nonviolent Resistance. Journal of Democracy 31 (3): 69–84.
soc-mov-06-c1.quote: Among the 565 campaigns that have both begun and ended over the past 120 years, about 51 percent of the nonviolent campaigns have succeeded outright, while only about 26 percent of the violent ones have.
soc-mov-06-c1.claim: About 51 percent of the nonviolent campaigns succeeded outright, against about 26 percent of the violent ones.

soc-mov-06-c2.text: Office for National Statistics (2025). Population estimates for the UK, England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland: mid-2024. Office for National Statistics.
soc-mov-06-c2.quote: The population of the UK continued to grow in the year to mid-2024, reaching an estimated 69.3 million people (69,281,400).
soc-mov-06-c2.claim: The ONS estimated the UK population at 69.3 million in mid-2024, so in the UK it would mean about 2.4 million people active at once.

soc-mov-06-c2.text: Erica Chenoweth (2020). Questions, Answers, and Some Cautionary Updates Regarding the 3.5% Rule. Carr Center for Human Rights Policy, Harvard Kennedy School.

soc-mov-06-c2.claim: Bahrain's uprising of 2011–2014 appears to have failed decisively despite over 6 percent participation at its peak; the regime relied on outside forces, including Saudi troops.

soc-mov-06-c3.text: Erica Chenoweth (2020). The Future of Nonviolent Resistance. Journal of Democracy 31 (3): 69–84.
soc-mov-06-c3.quote: Since 2010, less than 34 percent of nonviolent revolutions and a mere 8 percent of violent ones have succeeded.
soc-mov-06-c3.claim: Since 2010, fewer than 34 percent have succeeded, though violent campaigns did even worse, at 8 percent.

soc-mov-06-c3.text: Christoph Dworschak (2023). Civil resistance in the streetlight: replicating and assessing evidence on nonviolent effectiveness. Comparative Politics (White Rose Research Online).

soc-mov-06-c3.claim: Christoph Dworschak found its main results highly sensitive to variable selection, to cases that may have been missed (a "streetlight effect"), and to omitted variable bias.

soc-mov-07-c1.claim: A Pew Research Center analysis counted more than 44 million #BlackLivesMatter tweets from nearly 10 million distinct users between July 2013 and March 2023.
